library-annual-review.summary: The Riverside Library Network had 412,000 visitors in 2025, up from 368,000 in 2024, mainly thanks to two branches that opened until 9 pm on weekdays. Digital loans rose 22% to 156,000 while physical loans stayed flat at about 610,000. The $7.4 million budget went mostly to staff (58%) and the collection (19%), and a $350,000 city grant paid for self-service kiosks. Programmes were in demand: 2,300 children in the homework club and 640 adults completing the digital skills course. The main problems are 17% staff turnover, vacant manager posts and an unreliable mobile van. For 2026 the board approved repairing or replacing the van, opening a tenth branch in Northgate and testing Sunday opening at the central library.

technical-load-test.summary: At 1x and 2x production traffic the checkout service v3.2 met its 800 ms p99 objective (410 ms and 690 ms). At 3x the database connection pool (50 per instance) ran out after 11 minutes, giving a 2.7% error rate and latencies above 3 seconds for 6% of requests. Raising the pool to 80 and adding a read replica removed the errors (p99 720 ms); CPU stayed below 65%, so the database is the bottleneck.

long-with-digest.summary:
In 2025 the Riverside Library Network's 9 branches recorded 412,000 visitors, compared with 368,000 in 2024; the growth is attributed mainly to two branches that extended weekday opening to 9 pm from March. E-book and audiobook loans reached 156,000 (up 22%), while physical loans were flat at about 610,000. Of the $7.4 million operating budget, 58% went to staff and 19% to the collection; a one-off $350,000 city grant funded self-service kiosks in 5 branches, and energy costs fell 11% after the central library's heating was replaced in January.

Programme demand was high: 2,300 children registered for the homework club, 640 adults completed the digital skills course and the waiting list closed at 210. The mobile van served 14 villages fortnightly but missed 23 stops through breakdowns. Staff turnover stayed at 17%, with two branch manager posts vacant for over six months. For 2026 the board approved repairing or replacing the van, opening a tenth branch in Northgate by year end and trialling Sunday opening at the central library from April; the review advises measuring kiosk use before buying more.

sensitive-incident-report.summary: A stolen contractor VPN password let an attacker into the internal network on 9 October 2026 at 02:14. Over 3 hours the attacker copied a database export with the names, email addresses and hashed passwords of 18,400 customers; no payment card data was in it. An alert caught the transfer at 05:20, the account was disabled at 05:31 and all VPN passwords were reset that day. Multi-factor authentication for the VPN, planned for 2027, was enabled for every account on 11 October. The data protection authority was told on 11 October, within the 72-hour deadline, and customers were emailed on 12 October.
